---
title: "Case Study"
---

For our case study we looked at the article "The Unlikely Odds of Making it Big" by the Pudding. This data story has an interactive visualization that changes to show different layers of data as you scroll down. In the visualization, musical artists are represented by dots and they're separated into three rings making up a circle: the outer ring represents artists who played at small venues; the middle ring was artists who played medium venues; and the center was artists who played large venues. The visualization uses the size of the dots to represent the popularity of an artist based on what venue they played. It also uses the three different rings to demonstrate the massive difference in the amount of artists who are able to play smaller venues versus those who are able to play larger capacity venues. The story uses this visualization to support the overall point that the vast majority of bands don't succeed in 'making it big'. There is also another visualization that shows a timeline of the venues bands played over the course of their careers. The venues are represented by dots, and their size as well as their color corresponds to their capacity. This visualization shows the progression in the size of venue played by some bands, and how long it took for different artists to start playing larger venues. This visualization works effectively with the previous visualization by adding in time as a variable and focusing on a small group of specific bands. These visualizations are simple and use color and size to effectively communicate trends in data. This data story could potentially benefit from examining more variables that might correlate to how successful a band could be, but overall it tells a clear and concise story.
